title: Sidecar nudge mode sketch
content:
Background / one-liner:

I want a lightweight, optional sidecar layer — a "nudge" surface that runs alongside main LLM responses and offers micro-interactions: clarifying questions, short rewrites, quick source citations, and low-cost alternative responses. The sidecar should be cheap to run (small-model, low-context) and opt-in per user or route.

Why this?
- Product problem: Long responses are hard to triage; users often want a quick clarification or a shorter rewrite without re-sending the whole prompt.
- Economies: If we can satisfy many micro-asks with a tiny sidecar model, we avoid spinning up heavyweight calls and save tokens/cost for the customer.
- Differentiation: Developer-facing control to enable a thin interactive layer with its own SLOs (fast, cheap) is a unique operational primitive for Redwood.

Hypothesis:
- H1: For 35–50% of follow-up micro-asks (clarify, shorten, cite), a sidecar micro-response will be sufficient and cheaper than full LLM re-invocation.
- H2: Sidecar adoption will increase perceived responsiveness of apps, reducing visible complaint/latency metrics by 10–20% in early pilots.

Core ideas / behaviors to support:
- Inline clarifier: short clarifying question before larger generation ("Did you mean X or Y?").
- Rewrite/summarize: 1–2 sentence concise variants or TL;DR for long answers.
- Quick cite: try to produce a 1–2 line attribution or pointer when sources are available.
- Suggest alternatives: cheaper/higher fidelity toggle (micro vs full).
- Seamless fallback: when sidecar can't confidently answer, it signals and forwards to the main model.

User stories (prioritized):
- As a user, I want a short rephrase of a long answer so I can quickly scan it. (AC: <30 tokens, latency <150ms p50 on sidecar)
- As a dev, I want to enable sidecar per-route with a per-minute budget so sidecar calls don't blow my bill.
- As a product manager, I want metrics showing % of micro-asks resolved by sidecar vs forwarded.
- As an engineer, I need a clear fallback policy so sidecar failures don't degrade main app.

Acceptance criteria / minimal viable surface:
- Config API: per-route boolean enable + budget-per-minute and max-output-tokens.
- SDK: one-line opt-in flag in client request e.g., "sidecar: {enabled: true, mode: 'nudge'}".
- Runtime: cheap model pool (quantized 4-bit) deployed with <150ms p50 on target region for 32-token outputs.
- Observability: sidecar-specific metrics (calls, resolved, forwarded, errors, avg latency, cost estimate) in Console.
- Rollout: feature gate + canary (5% traffic) with easy disable.

Telemetry / metrics to track:
- sidecar.calls, sidecar.resolved_rate, sidecar.forward_rate, sidecar.avg_latency_ms, sidecar.cost_per_call_estimate
- downstream app metrics: follow-up full-model calls per session, token consumption delta, user engagement for flows with sidecar enabled

Experiment design (A/B):
- Cohort A: routes with sidecar off (control).
- Cohort B: routes with sidecar on, default config.
- 4 week window, primary metric: reduction in full-model follow-ups per session; secondary metrics: sidecar resolved_rate, average latency, cost delta.

Edge cases / risks:
- Sidecar hallucination hazard: producing confident but wrong short answers is worse than none. Mitigation: low confidence -> explicit "I might be wrong" tag + forward. Use conservative decoding and lower temp.
- Billing confusion: customers may not expect new small calls. Mitigation: clear console billing breakdown and quota defaults.
- SLAs: sidecar should never increase tail latency for main responses. Must run asynchronously or be cancellable.

Runtime / infra notes (quick):
- Sidecar pool: small models (65–120M) on CPU or small-GPU instances. Quantized model line that loads fast.
- Invocation pattern: run sidecar opportunistically in parallel with main LLM? Prefer lazy: kick sidecar for explicit micro-asks or when client UI requests "short" button. If parallel, need to ensure CPU/GPU contention isolation.
- KV / prefix cache: sidecar should read read-only session prefix (last 2 turns) to keep context cheap; avoid warmups that drive cost.
- Routing policy: prioritize sidecar on dedicated small-instance fleet; fallback to main model variant if sidecar rate-limited.

API sketch (very rough):
POST /v1/responses
payload: { prompt, route, options: {sidecar: {enabled: true, mode: "nudge", max_tokens: 32, budget_per_minute: 1000}}}
Response: { main: <maybe null if deferred>, sidecar: {status: "resolved"|"forwarded"|"skipped", text: "...", confidence: 0.72 } }
Notes: start with opt-in parameter; don't change default behavior.

UX notes / product flows:
- Toggle: per-user toggle in app settings + per-route feature flag for devs.
- UI affordances: "Shorten" button next to long responses; hovering reveals sidecar micro-suggestion; explicit "Expand to full" if forwarded.
- Visual: small pill labelled "Quick" with latency estimate (e.g., 120ms). If forwarded, change to "Expanded" with spinner.

Rollout plan / safety:
- Phase 0: internal dogfood, sidecar on for internal apps only, measure resolved rate and hallucination rate.
- Phase 1: gated beta customers + 5% canary on hosted API routes.
- Phase 2: public opt-in feature, console controls, and default-off for existing customers.
- Safety knobs: per-account sidecar cap, auto-disable on hallucination rate > X%, and manual admin kill-switch.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What exact model family for sidecar? (ask research: 65M vs 120M tradeoffs) @Maya
- Should sidecar run synchronously for certain UX flows (e.g., "shorten" button) vs async background hints?
- Cost model: how to price sidecar calls; share tokens vs separate line item? Finance input needed.
- Can we leverage existing KV cache to avoid additional context tokens for sidecar? Engineering input needed.

Implementation quick sketch / tickets:
- REDW-814: sidecar feature flag + route config
- REDW-820: SDK param and client behavior
- REDW-822: runtime small-model fleet + SLOs
- PR #998: initial runtime changes to allow concurrent small-model pool

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep expectations low on Day 1; this is an ops + UX product not new SOTA model work.
- Focus on metrics that matter to customers (dollars/token saved, latency improvement for common flows).
- Prototype with existing distilled open models to get early numbers before investing in quantized fleet.

Sample quick UX copy:
- "Quick view (0.12s): concise answer and alt suggestions"
- "Not sure? expand for full answer"

References / links:
- Slack thread: #product-sidecar-discuss (see linked_artifacts)
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/998
- Linear: REDW-814

-- end of sketch --

(rough, intentionally terse — will flesh out acceptance tests and a small experiment plan after initial numbers from prototype)
summary: Personal scratchpad: lightweight sidecar 'nudge' layer to handle micro-asks (clarify, shorten, cite) with cheap small-model calls, API sketch, runtime notes, UX ideas, experiment plan and open questions.
